implementation: First-receive HeadCall decoding needs no sender Rust object or full source store; it validates explicit UTF-8 windows, compound payloads, reachable projected nodes and source references.
HeadReply encoding and decoding validate the issued operation, all outcome branches, projected diagnostics and fixes, and terminal overflow consistency.
HeadDelegation exclusively borrows its parent Budget. An explicit transport reserve separates parent framing capacity from child execution capacity before work starts (R041).
Settlement records actual child usage once, including after a local stop. Unsettled Drop stops parent reuse; reserved capacity is not falsely reported as consumed work.
Already-issued source windows are counted by interval union within the child and not charged again to the parent; Depth merges as an absolute peak, while other resources accumulate.

The actual dynamic parser callback runs through raw NDF request and response bytes and produces the same complete tree as native execution; that dynamic tree also roundtrips through its portable codec.
